verdict.root_cause: Around 17:19 UTC checkoutservice stopped completing PlaceOrder requests: order-start lines keep arriving through 17:23:17, but no request after 17:19:07 reaches payment confirmation, email, or order publish, and checkoutservice logs no errors at all [tr_9fea75aec3e6]. paymentservice sees none of those charges - its logs stop at 17:16:42 with every prior receipt paired to a sub-millisecond completion, so charges stopped arriving rather than being processed slowly [tr_3391d631f80b]. The block therefore sits in a pre-charge hop. Of those hops, cartservice, currencyservice and productcatalogservice are closed sub-millisecond spans through 17:12, while the only hop flagged as degrading in all five sampled traces is shippingservice/GetQuote and its internal HTTP call to quoteservice, already 20-25% of trace self-time before onset [tr_85d28d498e0b]. Best reading: the quote hop became unresponsive at ~17:19, leaving checkoutservice blocked in-flight with spans never closing - which also explains the span-derived traffic gaps and the 8.9% mean / 67% peak error ratio as waits time out [tr_5fcac3511390], and why quoteservice and shippingservice only alerted at 17:22:45.
verdict.reasoning: The mode is silent hanging, not loud failure: checkoutservice is alive and accepting work but never advances past the pre-payment stage [tr_9fea75aec3e6], and the next downstream receives nothing [tr_3391d631f80b]. That pair places the blocking wait upstream of the charge call, inside checkoutservice's outbound fan-out. Elimination narrows it: the other pre-charge dependencies are fast closed spans, adservice and recommendationservice are not in the subtree, and the sole flagged degrading hop is the quote path [tr_85d28d498e0b]. Hangs rather than errors fit the volatile, bursty error ratio and the genuine no-sample intervals, since spans that never close produce no call samples [tr_5fcac3511390]. Both change queries returned empty and self-report windows starting at onset and running forward, so they exclude concurrent and follow-on changes but say nothing about pre-incident ones [tr_517bb1d1f417]. Confidence is low: no dispatch observed quoteservice or shippingservice directly, and the trace sample ends at 17:12:27, before the stall.
open_questions: No dispatch queried quoteservice or shippingservice at all; the attribution rests on elimination plus a pre-stall latency signal, not direct observation during the stall.
Both change-history windows start at onset and run forward, so any pre-incident deploy, config push or flag flip on any service remains unchecked [tr_517bb1d1f417].

No trace evidence covers 17:19 onward, so the open span that is actually blocking PlaceOrder was never identified [tr_85d28d498e0b]; cartservice also has no usable metrics in either window [tr_52e65f3d3eca].

alternatives.root_cause: shippingservice itself is hung - its own handler or HTTP client blocks rather than quoteservice being slow.
alternatives.why_not: The trace analysis localises the degrading hop to shippingservice's outbound HTTP call to quoteservice rather than to shippingservice self-time [tr_85d28d498e0b], but nothing directly observed either service, so this is only just below.

alternatives.root_cause: checkoutservice exhausted its own outbound connection or thread resources, so requests enter and queue without any dependency being at fault.
alternatives.why_not: No exhaustion diagnostics or error lines appear in checkoutservice logs and order starts continue at a steady rate [tr_9fea75aec3e6]; no saturation metric was ever queried, so it is admitted but unsupported.

alternatives.root_cause: A pre-incident config change on the quote or shipping path (e.g. a timeout or endpoint value) is the actual mechanism, with the wrong value breaking the call.
alternatives.why_not: The change queries never covered the hours before onset, so no such record was seen [tr_517bb1d1f417]; a wait is the observed failure, which reads as latency regardless of what started it.

proposal.expected_effect: No action proposed, so no effect is expected. What should happen next is observation, not remediation: a trace/log query against quoteservice and shippingservice covering 17:19:00 onward, and a change-history query on a window that *ends* at 17:19 rather than starting there. If the quote hop is truly the block, those queries would show either shippingservice GetQuote spans open past 17:19 with no quoteservice child completion, or quoteservice logs stopping/erroring at ~17:19 — the same signature paymentservice shows at 17:16:42 [tr_3391d631f80b], but one hop earlier.
proposal.if_wrong: This abstention is wrong if the stall is in fact a pure process-state hang in quoteservice that a restart would clear, and the delay in restarting extends customer-visible checkout failure. Two observations would show that: quoteservice logs or traces during 17:19-17:23 showing accepted requests with no completions and no error output, and no pre-17:19 change record for quoteservice. Either of those arriving would convert this into a restart_service proposal on quoteservice. Note also that the effect of a restart here is only weakly observable from the evidence we hold: checkoutservice error ratio is the nearest signal [tr_5fcac3511390], but it is highly volatile (sd of the same order as the mean) and has genuine traffic gaps, so a short post-restart window could not cleanly distinguish recovery from noise — a further reason not to act blind.
proposal.risk: The two candidate actions both fail their preconditions, and acting anyway carries real cost. restart_service requires evidence pointing at process state; no dispatch queried quoteservice or shippingservice at any point, and the only signal against them is a 5-8ms pre-stall latency contribution at 20-25% of trace self-time [tr_85d28d498e0b] — elevated but, as that same result records, far below stall magnitude. A restart discards in-process state and is irreversible; if the block is actually elsewhere (an unidentified open span after 17:19, which no trace evidence covers [tr_85d28d498e0b]) the restart destroys the hung-process state that would have identified the real culprit, and the incident continues with its best diagnostic gone. rollback_image and revert_config both require a named deploy or config change inside the window; no such change is named for any service, and both change-history windows are mis-specified — they begin at onset and run forward, so the hours before 17:19 are simply unchecked [tr_517bb1d1f417]. Proposing a rollback on an unrecorded prior image would be acting on an assumption the evidence explicitly does not support.
proposal.blast_radius: None from this proposal. For the record, had a restart been proposed on quoteservice, its inbound edge is shippingservice/GetQuote, which is called synchronously inside checkoutservice PlaceOrder [tr_85d28d498e0b]; a recreate would reset those connections and so be visible to shippingservice, checkoutservice, frontend and loadgenerator, i.e. the whole order path that is already failing.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical, ten services alerting within two minutes starting at checkoutservice and fanning out — this cannot be dismissed. Origin at checkout/frontend with downstream spread is consistent with several causes, so no prior is honest yet.
